title: AI is not the most important skill of the future #ai #artificialintelligence #tech #future
transcript: I'm convinced that AI is not the most important skill of the future. I was one of 15 people that Microsoft invited to their headquarters for private demos and presentations, and it made me realize that we're all focusing on the wrong thing. The problem with work today is the manufactured urgency to do everything. The author of Open to Work calls this the more better faster culture. >> We have really shrunk what humans do at work to be about efficiency above all else. So many jobs are more better faster, more better faster, more better faster. Now we're being told to learn AI to do more better and faster again. And most of us are going to learn these skills just to be safe, just to survive, because the future feels uncertain. But eventually everyone will have access to the same tools. So the difference won't be the tools that you have. It'll be the intelligence you bring. AI can do more, AI can do things faster, but it can't do things better. It's a tool for a volume and efficiency, not a replacement for quality. We feel worried because AI speeds up the visible parts of work, writing code, building a spreadsheet, or making a design. But what makes things better are the invisible skills we've been undervaluing for so long, our ability to think clearly, speak well, invent what doesn't exist, make bold decisions, and to stay human in a world that keeps pushing us to be mindless robots. We've seen that movie before. And here's the thing, we already notice when these skills are missing. We notice the person who gets all their ideas from AI, the person who lets AI write everything for them, even the person who lets AI make their decisions. They're accumulating cognitive debt that will crush them. AI is not the most important skill of the future because it's exposing the skills that make a difference. There is no great replacement, only a great rebalancing.
